Hi Lina / Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick written recap from our side so we all have the same next steps. High-level notes below, plus action items at the end.

Top pain points you reiterated:
- Customer-facing inference latencies spike on peak traffic windows (retail search & chat) causing degraded user experience.
- Current infra costs are rising due to incorrect batching and lack of KV cache reuse.
- Security: requirement to keep PII off third-party shared inference endpoints (must run in VPC or dedicated environment).

Aurora goals we captured:
- P95 tail latency target: <= 200ms for short-chat queries (~128 tokens); goal to hit <=120ms for 32–64 token responses on peak traffic.
- Sustained throughput target: ~250 qps (concurrent short requests), burst to 700 qps during peak events.
- Support models with up to 8k context windows; prefer quantized weights for cost reduction.
- SOC2 + customer-managed KMS + audit log retention for 90 days.

Suggested topology (high level):
- Dedicated Redwood Dedicated pool in us-west with autoscaling to handle baseline 250 qps, burst via reserved burst capacity and cross-region fallback to us-east.
- VPC peering + Private control plane; model pinned to a tested quantized 8-bit runtime.
- KV prefix caching for chat sessions to avoid repeated decoding for the first N tokens.

Open technical assumptions we used in the call (Diego will confirm in follow up):
- We estimated 4xA100-equivalent nodes for baseline 250 qps for a 13B dense model with int8; exact numbers vary by model and token length.
- For the latency targets, we assumed average request lengths of 40 tokens and response lengths of 60 tokens.

Attachments: I attached the short metrics screenshot you shared and a draft proposal (redwood-proposal-AU.pdf) for internal planning.

Next steps / owners:
- Diego: send a short technical deep-dive with concrete sizing and a recommended initial PoC topology (by Wed 04/07).
- Rachel: share sandbox credentials and a short test plan template for performance runs (by Thu 04/08).
- Lina: confirm the customer data classification for the PoC (PII vs non-PII) and availability windows for load tests (by Thu 04/08).
- Marcus: Will schedule a 60-minute PoC kickoff once Diego's sizing is shared.

If I missed anything obvious, flag it back. Thanks again — excited to get a focused PoC running.

Best,
Marcus

Thanks Marcus — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency targets: our internal SLA for chat is p95 <= 150ms for the commerce flow (short prompts) — we said 120ms as a stretch goal. Can you confirm whether the 120ms estimate assumes single-token streaming or aggregated response time?

2) Throughput: 250 qps baseline is correct; bursts are typically 600–800 qps for 3–5 minutes during promotions. Peak traffic pattern: 30% write (chat new queries), 70% read/context retrieval.

3) Data classification: PoC will use production-like non-PII synthetic data first; if PoC goes well, we will proceed to a guarded PII test under an IPAA agreement.

4) We will need the security questionnaire for our InfoSec team. Do you have a preferred doc? Also prefer to see SOC2 Type II report and KMS integration plan.

Happy to lock the PoC kickoff window; Thurs 04/08 morning PT looks good for our infra folks.

Lina

Lina — quick technical follow-up with concrete sizing and trade-offs. Copying Marcus and Rachel.

Summary of recommended PoC topology (short):
- Model: start with a 13B dense model (quantized int8) with 8k context enabled. We will also test a 7B quantized variant for cost/latency trade-offs.
- Runtime: Redwood inference runtime with KV caching enabled for chat sessions. Streaming responses enabled (producer-side flush set to 50ms).
- Nodes: baseline cluster: 4 nodes (A100 equivalent, 80GB BF16 / int8 runtime). Baseline should handle ~260 qps for 40-token inputs + 60-token outputs with p95 ~130–170ms depending on prompt variability.
- Burst: autoscaler configured with reserved burst + optional warm standby (2 nodes) to cover short 600–800 qps bursts; fallback region (us-east) for larger events.
- Network: VPC peering, direct path for inference traffic, TLS + mTLS for control plane.
- Security: KMS integration (customer-managed keys) + audit logs exported to your secure S3 bucket; SOC2 artifacts ready on NDA.

Notes on latency math / knobs:
- Tokenization + model forward pass dominate CPU/GPU time — optimizing prompt templates and prefix caching reduces per-request tokens by ~25% in our experience.
- Quantization to int8 typically reduces memory and improves throughput by 1.6–2.0x depending on operator coverage; some small latency variance on tail.

Proposed PoC plan (two-week):
Week 1: baseline deployment in your dedicated Redwood pool, run synthetic load to validate p95 targets at 250 qps; iterate on batching and streaming window.
Week 2: run customer-like traffic (synthetic session replay), validate burst behaviour, security sign-offs, evaluate 7B vs 13B cost/latency.

Data required from Aurora for sizing run:
- Representative traffic trace for 24-hour period (anonymized).
- A set of 200 canonical prompts (short chat + commerce search) for eval.

I will attach a short spreadsheet with initial perf numbers; Marcus / Rachel — see attached. Happy to jump on a quick 30–40m call Thurs morning to walk through.

Diego
